subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native memory trust and provenance contract should OpenClaw expose for durable memory before this feature is implemented?
rationale: The issue crosses security policy, persisted schema, plugin SDK/API compatibility, retrieval semantics, and operator review behavior, so automation should not choose the trust model or migration boundary alone.

options.title: Design native trust/provenance contract first
options.body: Define source authority, persisted metadata, migration behavior, SDK/config shape, retrieval gates, and review/expiration semantics before queuing implementation.

options.title: Scope to provenance foundation only
options.body: Treat source attribution/provenance issues as the first milestone and defer trust weighting, review gates, and expiration policy to follow-up design.

options.title: Route to external memory plugin only
options.body: Use the world-model or similar plugin approach as the experiment surface, accepting that OpenClaw core durable memory remains without native trust enforcement for now.

recommendation.title: Design native trust/provenance contract first
recommendation.body: Define source authority, persisted metadata, migration behavior, SDK/config shape, retrieval gates, and review/expiration semantics before queuing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to the memory-host SDK contract and prior issue review, which are central to deciding the public memory trust boundary.
